Home education (Home instruction; Homeschooling). Schooling provided either as an alternative to formal education or for homebound persons.
Family education. Education within and by the family.
Temperature (Atmospheric temperature; Temperature control; Water temperature)
Technical school teachers (Technical teachers; Vocational school teachers)
Iran. Use for events before 1979. Otherwise use Iran, Islamic Republic.
Dual economy. Economy in which a modern, capital-intensive sector coexists with an impoverished, traditional sector.
One teacher schools (Multigrade teaching; Multiple class teaching)
Ecological research (Ecological analysis). Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "ecology".
Ecology (Environmental biology). Use for the study of relationships between living organisms and their natural environment.
Mixed economy. Economy in which elements of government control are intermingled with market elements in organizing production and consumption.
Western Samoa. For events after September 1997, use Samoa.
Oceania (Melanesia; Pacific Islands; Polynesia; South Pacific)
Economics of science (Economics of research; Economics of technology)
Educational equipment (Academic equipment; School equipment; School supplies; Teaching equipment)
Part time employment. Employment on a regular basis for hours substantially shorter than the standard hours.
Full employment. Situation where all persons seeking employment have been provided with paid positions.
Managers (Administrators; Executive personnel; Middle grade personnel; Planners)
Humanities education (Humanities). Studies dealing with man as the central concern, e.g. literature, history, philosophy, and modern and classical languages.
Child psychology. From birth to adolescence.
Academic fraud (Academic misconduct; Accreditation fraud; Certification fraud; Examination fraud; False credentials; Forged diplomas; Student cheating)
Bullying (Peer abuse; Peer harassment; School bullying)
Education. Process by which one develops abilities, attitudes and other forms of behaviour considered to have value in the society in which one lives. Use more specific descriptor.
Educational anthropology. Application of anthropological concepts and methods to the study of educational institutions and processes.
Comparative education. Comparative study of current educational theory and practice in different countries.
Educational interaction process (Interaction process analysis). Observation of student behaviour in response to various teaching attitudes.
Educational models. Representation of an educational concept or system in a two or three-dimensional diagram or a mathematical or other analogous form.
Access to education. Conditions, circumstances or requirements governing admittance to educational institutions or programmes.
Educational priority areas. Regions, localities, etc., in need of special educational action.
Universal education (Education for all; Equal education; Equal opportunity in education). System of education extending opportunities to all.
Leisure and education (Leisure education). Organized activities intended to help individuals or groups use non-work time in a manner conducive to physical and mental well-being.
Illiteracy. Relates to the problem. Provision for resolving it should be handled by the "literacy" descriptors.

School closure (Closed schools; Educational disruption). Refers to both permanent or temporary school closures. The latter can be due to crisis situations such as natural disaster, armed conflict or epidemics.
Multilingual education. The use of two or more languages in education, which may include the mother tongue.

Alternative education (Anticurriculum movement; Deschooling; Educational alternatives). General term for schemes which offer an alternative to traditional institutional education or for movements which reject the notion of formal schooling.
Bilingual education. Encouragement of bilingualism through the teaching of regular courses in both the national language and a second language.
Intercultural education (Bicultural education; Crosscultural education; Multicultural education)
Educational opportunities. Availability of educational provision.

Computer uses in education (Educational computing). The use of computers for instruction, testing, student/pupil personnel services, school administrative support services, etc. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Education and culture. Taking into consideration of cultural factors in the educational process.

Curriculum development (Curriculum design; Curriculum improvement; Curriculum innovation; Curriculum planning; Curriculum reform; Curriculum reorganization). Systematic process of producing new curricula or improving existing ones. Involves setting out aims, content, methods, evaluation procedures.
Educational innovations. Changes in objectives, content or methods initiated, as a rule, in experimental situations.
Educational reform (Educational change; Educational renewal). Change planned or in process of implementation to a major part of a national system of education.
Democratization of education (Educational expansion). Policy of ensuring equality of educational opportunity in order to achieve universal education.
School integration (Educational integration; School desegregation; School segregation). Refers to ethnic groups, covers also negative aspect of segregation.

Global citizenship education (GCED; International cooperation education; International education; International understanding education; Values education). Global citizenship education aims to empower learners of all ages to assume active roles, both locally and globally, in building more peaceful, tolerant, inclusive and secure societies.

Educational development (Advancement of education). Developmental change of one or more characteristics of the educational system variables in a positive direction in terms of some valued criterion. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Educational policy. Official statements of goals to which the system of education is directed.
Educational trends. Changes in educational movement, either past or future, which occur in response to social, economic or environmental trends.
Educational indicators. Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of educational policy.
Educational objectives (Educational aims; Educational goals; Role of education). Intended or expected results of the educational process.
Educational strategies. Conversion of policy goals into operational terms, including some indication of alternative paths to reach these goals.
Study abroad (Cross-border education; Training abroad; Transnational education)
Economics of education. Techniques of economics applied to educational systems.
Enrolment (Educational registration). The total number of individuals registered as participants in a programme or activity.
Educational choice (Choice of education; Choice of educational institution; Choice of school; Choice of university)
Educational needs. At the level of educational systems.
School mapping (School distribution; School location). Planning further provisions of educational establishments in terms of demographic and geographical factors.
Teacher supply. Planning of manpower provision.
Educational efficiency (Educational cost effectiveness; Educational performance). Degree to which educational systems are successful in optimizing the educational input/output relationship.
Exchange programmes (Educational exchange). Provide systematically for the exchange of students or teachers between institutions.
Instructional programmes. Outline of procedures, courses and subjects to be provided by an educational institution over a given period of time.
Educational demand. Consumer demand for education.
Educational wastage. Effects of the associated problems of repetition and dropping out.
Education and development. Refers to the integration of education into the development process.
Education and employment (Education labour market relationship)
Transition from school to work (Entry into working life)
Educational forecasting (Educational futures). Long term projection of educational development. May include design of scenarios for educational systems.
Enrolment ratio. Enrolment as percentage of relevant age group.
Academic freedom. Liberty of educational institutions to decide courses and research, and of teachers to teach subjects, without outside coercion.
Accreditation (education) (Accredited schools). Recognition and approval of the academic standards of an educational institution by some external, impartial body of high public esteem.
Scientific freedom (Freedom of research; Freedom of science; Freedom of scientific research; Research freedom)
Educational administration. Relating to part or the whole of the educational system.
Educational articulation. Between levels of education or types of school.
Educational assistance (Educational missions; Training assistance). Provided by specialist missions to countries under international programmes.
Educational associations. Voluntary bodies concerned with the administration of education.
Educational autonomy (Educational self management; School based management). Arrangements giving educational establishments at any level a degree of autonomy in administrative and programme matters.
Educational governing boards. Entrusted with some degree of control over managing the affairs of private and public institutions.
Educational coordination. Coordination of different agencies and organizations concerned with education.
Educational foundations (Educational trusts). Provide grants or funds to finance research, services, facilities, equipment.
Government educational bodies (Departments of education; Ministries of education)
Regional educational bodies. Intergovernmental bodies grouping a number of countries.
Examination boards. Organize the setting and marking of examinations and the recording of results.

Admission requirements (Academic admission; Admission criteria; Early admission; Educational admission; School admission; Student admission; Student selection). Conditions (examination certificates, proof of skills, etc.) of entrance to courses of study, further study, training, etc.
Educational grants (Educational awards; Educational vouchers; Student grants; Study grants)

Educational guidance (Educational counselling; Guidance service; School leaving guidance). Advising pupils or students on their educational progress, on career opportunities, or personal difficulties or anxieties.
Educational management (Academic management; School administration; School management). Use to mean the management of educational establishments.
School leaving (School leavers; School leaving age)
Scholarships. Reserve for school and undergraduate levels of education.
Fellowships. Award to continue studies to an advanced level.
Vocational guidance (Career counselling; Career guidance; Occupational guidance). Help given to the individual inside or outside the school system in choosing a career or occupation.
Adult education (Polyvalent adult education). The offering of learning opportunities in professional and vocational development, personal development, and social development to adults.
Consumer education. Study of intelligent and effective methods of buying and using goods and services.
Workers education. The education of union members to improve their bargaining skills. Do not confuse with "adult education".
Community education (Social education). Enabling process through which children and adults receive a sense of identification with their community.
Correctional education (Prison education). Educational and vocational programmes provided for adults or youth in prisons or detention centres.
Higher education (Postsecondary education; Tertiary education; Third stage education; University education). Stage following secondary education, regardless of course duration or certificate awarded.

Informal learning (Informal education). The process of learning which goes on continuously and incidentally for each individual, outside the organized situation of formal or nonformal education. Do not confuse with "nonformal education".
Lifelong learning (Continuing education; Continuous learning; Lifelong education; Permanent education)
Out of school education (Parallel schooling). Institutions, programmes and activities for out of school youth and extra-curricular activities for those in school.

University extension (Extramural teaching). Extension activity of universities organizing local short or part time courses in academic subjects to adults other than its students, usually away from the campus.
Special needs education (Disabled education; Handicapped education; Special education). Education of students with special learning needs such as those with disabilities or learning difficulties.

Learning cities. A learning city mobilizes its resources in every sector to promote inclusive learning from basic to higher education for all its residents, and fosters a culture of learning throughout life.
Educational levels. Broad steps of formal educational progressions. Used as a classification in educational organization and statistics.

Basic education (Fundamental education). A broader concept than primary schooling, comprising early child education, adult literacy programmes, and a range of nonformal activities for children, young people and adults.
Educational systems (National educational systems). Arrangement into an organic whole of the interdependent institutions and programmes providing formal and nonformal education.
Extension education (Educational extension). Instructional activities of educational institutions directed to clientele outside immediate student body.
Nonformal education. Organized and systematic learning activity, often associated with work, provided outside the formal educational system.
Child rearing (Parenting; Traditional educational practices; Upbringing). Refers to a set of culturally and socially determined practices, customs and beliefs.
Early childhood education (ECCE; Early childhood care and education; Preprimary education; Preschool education). From birth to the age of 8. It refers to all aspects of a child's development.
Day nurseries (Daycare; Family daycare). Centres where young children may be left to be cared for, while the parents are at work or study. May include health and family services.
Mass education. A large-scale undertaking aimed at disseminating information to influence the opinion of the general public. May also be used in relation to the propagation of popular culture.
Compensatory education. For deprived or disadvantaged students.
Private education (Fee paying schools; Independent schools; Private schools)
Migrant education (Migrant child education; Nomad education). Refers to the education of migrant workers and their families.
Recurrent education. Periodic professional renewal, distinct from more general concept of lifelong education.
Traditional education. That provided by societies before or alongside the introduction of a formal educational system.
Primary education (Elementary education). From age five to eleven.
Public education (Public schools; State education; State schools)
Outdoor education. Utilization of the outdoor environment to promote experiential learning and enrich the curriculum.
Technical and vocational education (TVET; Technical and vocational education and training)
Universities (Colleges (USA); University colleges; University institutes). Institutions of higher education with legal right to confer degrees.
Technological institutes (Polytechnics; Technical colleges; Technical schools). Institutions of higher education with a strong orientation towards study and research in the technologies and sciences.
Evening schools (Evening colleges; Evening courses; Night schools)
Summer schools. Short course usually held at a university or college during the summer vacation.
Single-sex schools (Boys schools; Girls schools; Same-gender schools; Same-sex schools; Sex-segregated schools)
Associated schools. Relates to the UNESCO Associated Schools Project.
Teacher centres. Organized centres for teachers to meet, discuss, find resources and develop materials.
Community schools (Community colleges). Schools open beyond ordinary hours for use of students, their parents and the community.
Disadvantaged schools. Schools where activities, facilities or resources do not meet the basic educational needs of students.
Open universities (Radio universities). Higher education institutions with open admission that offer external degree programmes.
Nursery schools (Kindergarten; Preprimary schools). Institutions providing education for preschool children.
Teacher education schools (Colleges of education; Teacher colleges; Teacher training institutions; Teacher training schools)
Special schools (Special education centres). For disabled students.
Extracurricular activities (After school activities). Activities organized by the school, for which participation is generally not compulsory.

Core curriculum (Common core). Essential or basic parts of the curriculum of an educational institution that are studied by all its students even though each has a choice of optional subjects in addition.
Elective courses (Optional courses). Courses chosen freely by a student from among a number of alternatives.
Postgraduate courses (Postgraduate education). Courses of study or research at a higher education institution after completion of first degree requirements.
Integrated curriculum (Integrated education; Interdisciplinary curriculum). Systematic organization of curriculum content and parts into a meaningful pattern.

Modular instruction (Modular courses; Modular curriculum; Modular learning; Modular training). Organization of the curriculum or of instructional courses in self-contained units ('modules') designed for management by the learner.
Functional literacy. General concept of relating literacy to improved living conditions.
Art education. Use for drawing, graphics, painting, and sculpture.
Media education (Education for communication; Media literacy). Seeks to enable people to gain an understanding of the way the media act and operate in society, and critically analyze media messages.
Life skills (Basic learning needs; Basic life skills; Basic skills). The ability and readiness to face and solve demands and challenges of everyday life.

Information literacy (Information competency; Information fluency). Comprises the competencies to recognize information needs and to locate, evaluate, apply and create information within cultural and social contexts
Education for sustainable development (ESD; Education for sustainability)

Social and emotional learning (Socio-emotional learning). Process through which children and adults understand and manage emotions, set and achieve positive goals, feel and show empathy for others, establish and maintain positive relationships, and make responsible decisions.
Futures literacy. Skill that allows people to better understand the role of the future in what they see and do.
Holocaust education (Education about the Holocaust; Teaching and learning about the Holocaust)
Population education (Family life education; Family planning education). Do not confuse with "family education".

General technical education (Polytechnical education; Technology education). Provides knowledge about production principles and processes and practical skills needed for participation in productive work.
Speech education (Elocution education). Includes various aspects of oral communication such as discussion, conversation, debate, interpretative reading and drama.
Language instruction (Language education; Language learning; Language teaching)
Digital skills (Computer literacy; Digital literacy). Comprehension of the capabilities and applications of computers. May include the ability to use computers to solve problems.
Development education. Education on the issues of concern in the development process addressed to youth and adults in developed countries.
Technical teacher education (Technical teacher training; Vocational teacher training)

Inservice teacher education (Inservice teacher training). Designed to enable teachers to be retrained, or to obtain a higher level certificate, or even to be initially trained when already in the field.
Microteaching. An experimental teacher training method using small groups of students.
Management education (Business education). Educational programmes to increase managerial and supervisory skills of managers and management trainees.

Technical education (Technical training). Formal education designed to provide knowledge and skills underlying production processes with a wider connotation than vocational education at secondary or higher level.
Vocational education (Professional education). Formal education designed to prepare for skilled occupations.
Industrial education (Industrial training). All types of education related to industry including industrial arts and education for occupations in industry at all levels.
Foreign students (International students; Transnational students). Students not native to a particular country.
Academic teaching personnel (College teachers (USA); Faculty; Higher education teaching personnel; Lecturers; Tutors; University professors)
Educational administrators (Deans; Head teachers; Headmasters; Inspectors of education; Principals; Rectors)
Trainers (Training officers). Persons who direct the practice of skills toward immediate improvement in some art or task.
Trainees. Participants in vocational, administrative or technical training programmes for purpose of developing job related skills.
Slow learners (Educationally retarded; Low ability students; Mentally retarded students)
Gifted students (High achievers; Overachievers; Talented students)
Exceptional students. Covers atypical students of any kind.

Classroom techniques (Classroom arrangement; Classroom management). Techniques used in the classroom or in any other educational setting to create propitious learning conditions. Includes discipline, management, sitting arrangement.
Home study (Homework). Studying done at home outside school hours, including work on school assignments, community projects, or individual problems. Do not confuse with "Home education".

Competency based teaching (Competency based education; Performance based education). Refers to specific teaching skills of interacting with students in classrooms, based on the clear definition of the knowledge, skills and attitudes to be acquired. (IBE uses: competency-based education)

Study service (higher education). Optional or compulsory part of a programme of studies where credit is given for work off-campus in social or development services, local government, and industrial or other organizations.

Work experience programmes (Cooperative education (USA); Education and productive work; Sandwich courses (UK); Sandwich training (UK); Work study programmes). Instructional programmes providing for some part of the students' time to be spent in one of the sectors of production.
Activity learning (Activity methods; Experiential learning). Learning by doing.
Further training. Global term for training subsequent and complementary to initial training.
Electronic learning (E-learning; M-learning; Mlearning; Mobile learning; Online learning; Virtual learning). Online learning via the Internet or an intranet.
Blended learning (Hybrid learning). Learning approach that combines both remote learning and in-person learning

Vocational training (Job training; Occupational training). Training aiming at providing the skills, knowledge and attitudes required for employment in a particular occupation, or group of related occupations, in any field of economic activity.
Multimedia instruction (Media assisted education). Integration of more than one medium in a presentation or module of instruction.
Self instruction (Self teaching methods). Learning by oneself without the aid of a teacher.
Basic training. Specially organized training, given outside of production activities of an undertaking, and aimed at imparting the basic knowledge and skill required for a given group of occupations.
Retraining (Reskilling; Vocational rehabilitation). Training for a new occupation.
Inservice training (On the job training). Training acquired during employment.
Professional training (Training of professionals). Special instruction to develop skills needed to improve job performance of professional personnel, usually short term and job specific.
Remedial instruction (Remedial teaching). Designed to catch up with a lag in a given subject or field.
Computer assisted instruction (Computer assisted learning; Computer assisted teaching; Computer managed instruction)
Tutoring (Coaching). Private intensive teaching, usually of a single student.
Seminars (teaching method) (Student seminars). Meetings of a group of students engaged in research or advanced study under the direction of one or more leaders to discuss problems of mutual interest.
Teaching (Instruction; Teaching process). Technical aspects of the teaching process. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.

Distance education (Distance study; Distributed education; Distributed learning; Open learning systems). Education imparted at a distance through the use of information/communication technology: radio, TV, the telephone, correspondence, e-mail, videoconferencing, audioconferencing, cd-roms, or online.
Independent study (Individual study). Study carried out with a minimum or a complete absence of external guidance. Do not confuse with "individualized instruction".

Teaching methods (Didactics; Educational methods; Instructional methods; Teaching strategies; Teaching techniques). Patterns of teacher behaviour that are recurrent, applicable to various subject matters, characteristic of more than one teacher and relevant to learning.
Training. Systematic educative process by which one learns new skills.
Programmed instruction (Programmed courses; Programmed learning; Programmed materials)
Peer teaching (Peer tutoring). The practice of having students of the same or similar age assist with the instruction of other students who may need supplemental aid.
Academic standards (Educational standards). Criteria established by an educational institution to determine levels of student achievement.
Student evaluation (Educational assessment; Educational rating; Student appraisal; Talent identification)
Teacher effectiveness. Degree to which teachers are successful in satisfying their objectives, obligations and functions.
Equivalence between diplomas (Academic recognition; Mutual recognition of qualifications). Includes all levels.
Educational background (Background knowledge; Prior knowledge; Prior learning)
Diplomas (Educational certificates; Leaving certificates). Certificates of higher education with less weight than a degree.
Prior learning evaluation (Prior learning accreditation; Prior learning assessment; Prior learning recognition; Recognition of prior learning)
National qualifications framework. Instrument used to classify a country’s qualifications at different levels. Each level is defined by a set of learning outcomes expected at that level.
Aptitude tests. Instruments used to assess a combination of native and acquired abilities which are considered indicative of future performance.
Educational accountability. Being held responsible and answerable for specific results or outcomes of an activity (over which one has responsibility).
Educational relevance (Curriculum relevance). Applicability of what is taught to the needs and interest of students and society.
Academic achievement (Academic performance; Student achievement; Student progress)
Educational qualifications (Academic qualifications). Required conditions, usually academic, for a post.
Educational quality (Educational improvement). Degrees of excellence in meeting educational objectives. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Teacher evaluation (Teacher appraisal; Teacher effectiveness evaluation). Judging teacher performance based on established criteria.
Dropping out. Premature school leaving before completing a cycle or course already begun.
Open educational resources (OER; Open courseware; Open teaching/learning resources)
Audiovisual aids. Nonprint teaching materials and the equipment required for their display.
Teaching machines (Self instructional aids). Devices that mechanically, electrically or electronically present instructional programmes at a rate controlled by the learner's responses.
Media resource centres (Audiovisual centres; Media centres; Multimedia centres; Multimedia libraries)

Lesson plans (Lesson notes). A teacher's outline of what he hopes to accomplish with the students during a particular lesson. It may list aims, main teaching points, media and resources, teaching and evaluation methods, etc.
Educational software (Courseware). Computer software and accompanying documentation written for educational applications.
Teaching guides (Teacher books; Teacher guides). Manuals for teachers often accompanying textbooks.
Learning packages (Learning kits; Self instructional packages). Materials designed so that learners can learn from them without much help from a teacher: they are pre-recorded, stored teaching.
Educational technology. Theory and application of educational media in a systematic way.

Teaching materials (Educational materials; Educational media; Instructional materials; Teaching aids). Any printed and/or nonprinted material designed specifically for or used in instruction. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Formative evaluation. A type of assessment essentially used to modify and improve products, programmes or activities during their planning and development.
Summative evaluation. A type of evaluation that sums up the effects and effectiveness of a programme or activity once it is concluded.

Benchmarking (Comparative evaluation). Systematic and continuous evaluation of products, services, performances or methods against a standard or agreed upon point of reference in order to achieve excellence.
Accessibility (Accessible design; Barrier-free design; Universal design)
Comparative analysis (Comparative research). Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Evaluation (Appraisal; Assessment). Appraising or judging persons, organizations or things in relation to stated objectives, standards or criteria. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Science and society (Sociology of research; Sociology of science; Sociology of technology). Relations between science as human activity and as factor of change, and social structures.
Systems design (Systems analysis; Systems engineering). Development of an integrated method for producing a required article or performing a desired operation.
Quality control. Techniques, such as inspection and regulation, that are used to ensure a uniform and/or desired quality of performance or product.
Simulation models (Cybernetic models; Models; Simulation techniques). Use only in connection with research and planning.
Methodology. Study of the direction and implications of research methods and techniques, especially as to their logical basis.
Science administration (Research administration; Research management; Technological administration)
Fundamental research (Basic research; Free research; Pure research). Research designed to produce new understanding of basic underlying principles and processes.
Technology (Science and technology). The skills, knowledge, hardware, and procedures for providing useful goods and services.
High technology (Advanced technology; Frontier technologies; New technology)
Interdisciplinary research (Multidisciplinary research). Research which establishes conceptual and methodological relationships among various disciplines.
Digital divide (Digital gap). Disparities in access to, and use of information and communication technologies such as Internet, between as well as within countries.
Nanotechnology (Nanoscience). Research and engineering conducted at the nanoscale.
Open science (Open research). Combines various movements and practices aiming to make scientific knowledge openly available, accessible and reusable for everyone.
Applied research. Research which is designed to create a new technology.
Mission oriented research (Problem focused research). Research designed for the solution of a specific problem.
Research and development (Industrial research; R & D; Research and experimental development). Research directed towards the development of new products and processes.
Appropriate technology (Alternative technology; Intermediate technology). Technology adapted to the needs, production system, and natural resources of a given country.

Technology transfer (Horizontal technology transfer; Transfer of techniques; Vertical technology transfer). Access to new technology, both products and production techniques, as a key factor in the economic growth of developing countries.
Traditional technology (Endogenous technology). Techniques passed from generation to generation (although some modernized components or processes may be included).
Automation. The act or practice of using machines that need little or no human control, especially to replace workers.
Choice of technology. Deciding on labour intensive or capital intensive methods, choosing among various manufacturing processes, etc.
Science and development. Refers to the integration of science and technology into the development process.
Diffusion of technology (Diffusion of innovations). Transfer of a new technology from the first commercial user to a number of competing users.
Know-how transfer. Technical and managerial expertise necessary to implement a technology.
Scientific innovations (Inventions; Scientific discoveries; Scientific progress; Technical progress; Technological discoveries; Technological innovations)
Science finance (Research financing; Science financing; Technology financing)
Technology assessment (Technology evaluation). Refers to the examination and evaluation of the possible consequences of the introduction of new technologies.

Statistics (Statistical methodology; Statistical methods). Use when referring to the science of statistics. For collections of statistics, use "statistical data", or more specific descriptor, e.g. "educational statistics", etc.
Flow (Gas flow; Liquid flow; Water flow)
Wave mechanics. Includes wave equations and functions.
Cosmology (Cosmogony). Nature and origin of the universe.
Seismicity. Frequency and distribution of earthquakes.
Steppe. Vast treeless plains of South-eastern Europe and Siberia.
Sea ice (Floating ice; Ice packs; Icebergs)
Savannah. Treeless plains in tropical or subtropical regions.
Palaeogeography (Paleogeography). Historical reconstitution of the physical geography of past ages.
Oceanographic measurement (Bathythermographs; Salinity measurement; Sea water measurement)
Oceanographic research. Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "oceanography".
Plankton (Marine bacteria; Marine microorganisms; Phytoplankton; Zooplankton)
Sea water (Marine water; Sea water properties; Sea water quality)
Biogeography. Geographical distribution of animals and plants.
Regional geography (Area studies). Use for the study of the geographical features within an area as they interact to give the area a unique character.
Human geography (Cultural geography; Population geography). Relationship of geography and culture (population, institutions and technology).
Hydrometeorology. The study of the occurence, movement and changes in the state of water in the atmosphere.
Hydrological cycle (Water cycle). The continuous circulation of water through evaporation and precipitation.
Climate. Average weather of any region.
Weather modification (Artificial precipitation; Cloud seeding; Rain making; Weather control)
Hydrological research. Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "hydrology".

Water security. Capacity of a population to safeguard access to adequate quantities of water of acceptable quality for sustaining human and ecosystem health on a watershed basis, and to ensure efficient protection of life and property against water-related hazards – floods, landslides, land subsidence and droughts.
Transboundary waters (Transboundary aquifers; Transboundary groundwaters; Transboundary lakes; Transboundary rivers; Transboundary water resources; Transboundary watercourses)
Hydrology (Hydrography; Water sciences). The study of the waters of the earth, their circulation, distribution and properties.
Drainage basins (Catchment area; Catchment basins; Drainage area; Hydrological basins)

Water balance. The flow and storage in a hydrologic unit such as a drainage basin, a soil zone, a lake or reservoir and the relationship between evaporation, precipitation, runoff and the change in water storage.
Hydrosphere. That part of the earth that is water e.g. oceans, lakes and rivers.
Environmental impact assessment. An activity designed to identify, predict, interpret and communicate information concerning the environmental consequences of policies, projects etc.
Environmental indicators. Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of environmental policy.
Environmental ethics (Ecological ethics; Environmental philosophy; Ethics of nature). Ethical reflection relating to human interaction with the natural environment
Waste treatment (Sewage handling; Sewage treatment; Waste collection; Waste handling; Waste recycling)
Biological control. Control of undesirable insects, plants or animals by the introduction of predators, parasites, or diseases.
Water treatment (Chlorination; Fluorination; Water demineralization; Water purification)
Energy economics. Economics as it relates to the energy sector.

Eutrophication. Enrichment of water by nutrients, especially compounds of nitrogen and phosphorus, that will accelerate the growth of algae and higher forms of plant life, and thus deplete the oxygen level of water.
Transport safety (Air safety; Marine safety; Rail safety; Road safety; Traffic accidents)
Climate change adaptation (Adaptation to climate change). Initiatives and measures to reduce the vulnerability of natural and human systems against actual or expected climate change effects
Education in emergencies (Emergency education). Refers to the quality learning opportunities for all ages  in  situations  of  crisis
Dangerous materials (Dangerous goods; Explosives; Harmful substances; Hazardous materials; Poisons; Toxic substances)
Human activities effects (Environmental effects; Environmental impact)
Disaster risk reduction (Disaster mitigation; Disaster preparedness; Disaster prevention; Disaster reduction)
Biological adaptation. A genetically determined characteristic that enhances the ability of an organism to cope with its environment.
Ecosystem services. Benefits received by society thanks to the functioning of ecosystems.
Soil resources. Use to denote the availability of soil, mainly for cultivation.

Ecosystems (Biological communities; Food chains). The system of interdependent complex of plant and animal populations within a particular geographic content, generally an area of uniform environmental conditions.
Biosphere. That part of the earth, and the atmosphere surrounding it, which is able to support life.
Biomass energy (Bioenergy). Energy from the conversion of agricultural and forest residues, standing vegetation, energy crops, and wastes.
Biosphere reserves. Reserves created to ensure long-term survival of representative ecosystems, with their component plants and animals.
Biomes (Ecological regions). The largest land community region, e.g. tundra, savannah, grassland, desert, forest. Each biome may contain several ecosystems.
Biomass. The mass of organisms living in an animal or plant ecosystem.
Eugenics. Improvement of hereditary characteristics of a population or of a family by controlled or selective breeding.
Physiological effects (Fatigue (physiology); Stress (physiology)). Effects of electricity, chemicals, heat, pressure, etc. on the human body.
Space biology (Astrobiology). Use for the study of man or other earth life in outer space.
Genome (Genetic heritage; Human genome). Complete genetic repertoire of an organism.
Genes (DNA; Genetic code). The fundamental physical and functional unit of heredity, responsible for specific traits.
Bioethics. Study of social and ethical questions raised by development in biology and medicine.
Limnology (Freshwater biology). Study of living organisms in freshwater.
Trace elements. Elements combined in minute quantities in plant or animal tissues considered essential in physiological processes.
Biosynthesis. Production of molecules by a living cell which is essential feature of anabolism.
Biological research. Use for works dealing with research projects. For general scientific works, use "biology".
Biometrics. Statistical methods applied to biological problems.
Invasive species (Exotic species; Introduced species; Non-indigenous species; Non-native species)
Animal taxonomy (Zoological taxonomy). Classification of the species of animals.
Human species (Human beings; Humankind; Humans; Mankind)
Ethnobotany. Knowledge, uses and methods of management of plant resources by communities.
Plant taxonomy (Botanical taxonomy). Classification of the species of plants.
Occupational medicine (Occupational therapy). Medical care in its relation to work and the work environment.
Medical technology (Biomedical engineering; Biomedical technology; Laser medicine; Medical engineering; Nuclear medicine)
Preventive medicine (Disease prevention; Genetic screening; Screening for disease)
Medical rehabilitation (Aftercare (medical); Medical aftercare; Prosthetics; Rehabilitation)
Epidemiology. Study of the occurence and distribution of disease.
Narcotic drugs (Cannabis; Cocaine; Hallucinogenic drugs; Heroin; LSD; Opium; Psychotropic drugs)
Injuries. Includes fractures, wounds, burns, etc.
Infectious diseases (Bacterial diseases; Communicable diseases; Contagious diseases; Parasitic diseases)
Occupational diseases (Industrial diseases; Industrial medicine; Occupational health; Stress related diseases). Harmful effects of occupational activities and work environment on workers' health.
Mental deficiency (Intellectual disability; Mental disability; Mental retardation)

Acculturation (Cultural assimilation; Cultural integration; Enculturation). Phenomena which result when groups of individuals of different cultures come into continuous contact, with subsequent changes in the original cultural patterns of either or both groups.
Dominant cultures (Cultural dominance; Cultural hegemony; Cultural imperialism)
Cultural isolation. Relative lack of participation in the cultural system.

Cultural identity (Cultural alienation; Cultural identification; Ethnic identity). Denotes the correspondence which exists between a community (national, ethnic, linguistic, etc.) and its cultural life, as well as the right of each community to its own culture.
Civilization crises. Situation in which a civilization is fundamentally called into question.
Countercultures. Cultural system which develops in conflict with the prevailing culture.
Subcultures. Culture peculiar to a social group or category.
Scientific culture (Technical culture). Pattern of intellectual and social behaviour based on scientific knowledge.
Culture of poverty. A set of values, beliefs, attitudes and behaviour patterns which result from persistent marginalization and exclusion, and characterize the cultural milieu of the poor.
Culture of peace. A culture that promotes lifeways, patterns of belief, values and behaviour that foster peace-building and accompanying institutional arrangements.
Culture of work (Corporate culture; Culture of enterprise; Organizational culture)
Cultural minorities (Minority cultures). Group of persons belonging to a culture different from that of the majority of the society in which they live.
Cultural inequality. Disparity of levels of culture and access to it within a given society.
Cultural diversity (Cultural pluralism). Coexistence within society of culturally differentiated groups which maintain separate ways of life.

Cultural activities (Socio-cultural activities). All types of activities tending to enhance cultural life through cultural animation and cultural values promotion. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Digital preservation. Digital preservation consists of the processes aimed at ensuring the continued accessibility of digital materials.

Cultural action (Socio-cultural action). Efforts tending to develop culture in the broadest meaning of the term, with reference to community development, freedom of expression and free choice of life style.
Preservation of monuments (Historic cities preservation; Historic monuments preservation; Historic sites preservation)

Cultural property preservation (Conservation of cultural property; Cultural heritage preservation; Protection of cultural property). Refers to the conservation, preservation and restoration of cultural property, as well as to its protection against vandalism, theft and removal from country of origin.
Cultural property restitution (Cultural property traffic; Illicit trafficking of cultural property)
Cultural users (Audiences; Cultural consumers; Cultural consumption; Spectators)

Intangible cultural heritage (Intangible heritage; Living heritage). A set of living practices, knowledge and representations enabling individuals and communities to express themselves through systems of values and ethical standards. Use more specific descriptor if appropriate.
Document preservation (Book conservation; Book preservation; Document maintenance; Document restoration)
Documentary heritage. Valuable archive holdings and library collections of the world.
Cultural industry (Creative economy; Creative industries; Cultural goods; Cultural productions; Cultural services)
Preservation of works of art (Conservation of works of art)
Culture and development. Cultural dimension of the development process.
Cultural development. Process of development or progress in the cultural life of a community.
Dissemination of culture (Cultural communication; Cultural diffusion)
Cultural organizations (Cultural associations; Cultural foundations; Cultural institutions)
Cultural relations. Relations at both the international and intergroup level. Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Cultural indicators. Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of cultural policy.
Digital heritage. Consists of  unique  resources  of  human  knowledge  and  expression created digitally, or converted into digital form from existing analogue resources.
Ontology. The study of the essential characteristics of Being in itself apart from the study of particular existing things.
Epistemology. The theory or science of the method or grounds of knowledge.
Metaphysics. Includes philosophy of nature, philosophy of life, infinity, etc.

Traditional knowledge (Indigenous knowledge; Local knowledge). Body of facts developed and maintained by a distinct cultural group as a result of direct observation and practice, including the distinctive perspective and ideas inferred from these facts.
Religious behaviour (Psychology of religion; Religious fanaticism)
Cults. A particular form of religious worship, devotion to a particular person or thing.
Prehistory (Bronze age; Iron age; Stone age)
Human remains (Human Bone; Human Skeleton; Human skull; Skeletal remains). Use for the remains of any part of a human
Collective memory (Collective remembrance; Cultural memory; Historical memory; Social memory)
Archaeological sociology. Social anthropological interpretation of archaeological remains.
Palaeography (Paleography). The study of ancient scripts and their development as found in manuscripts.
Chronology (Historical chronology). The science of computing time or periods of time and of assigning events to their true dates.
Uncommonly taught languages (Less widely used languages)
Language preservation (Language maintenance; Language protection; Language revitalisation; Language revival; Language safeguarding)
Transliteration. Representation of a lexical item recorded in one writing system by means of the signs and symbols of another.
Ancient scripts (Hieroglyphics; Ideographic scripts; Pictographic scripts)
Languages (Language types; Language varieties; Linguistic diversity)
Psycholinguistics (Neurolinguistics). Study of the relationships between linguistic behaviour and psychological processes, including the process of language acquisition.
Sociolinguistics. Social and cultural functions of language.
Comparative linguistics (Synchronic linguistics). Study of language change and variation.
Etymology. Study of the origins and history of the form and meaning of words.
Ethnolinguistics. Study of language with reference to is cultural context.
Transcription. System of writing the sounds of a word in one language using the script of another language.
Indigenous languages (Autochthonous languages; Vernacular languages). The native speech or language of a particular country or district.
Contemporary literature. Literature of the 20th century.
Digital art (Cyber art; Electronic art; Media art). Art created using digital technologies.
Contemporary art. Art of the 20th-21st century.
Iconography. The branch of art history dealing with the identification, description, classification and interpretation of the subject-matter of the figurative arts.
Art styles. Use for individual art styles, such as Renaissance, Gothic, Baroque, Impressionism, etc.
Funerary monuments (Funerary sites; Gravestones; Mausoleums; Sepulchral monuments; Tombstones)
Traditional music (Folk music). Music distinctive of a certain region or ethnic group.
Film industry (Film distribution; Film production; Movie industry)
Museum laboratories (Conservation laboratories; Museum repair workshops)
Museum educational programmes (Educational function of museums)
Ecotourism (Ecological tourism; Green tourism; Sustainable tourism). Environmentally friendly and socially responsible tourism.
Participatory research (Participatory approach). Research approach that calls for interaction between the researchers and those among whom the research is conducted.
Behavioural sciences. Any science that studies human and animal behaviour in its physical and social environment by experimental and observational methods.
Social skills (Interpersonal skills; Social abilities; Social competence)
Cognition (Cognitive processes). The mental action or process of acquiring knowledge through thought, experience and senses.

Developmental psychology (Genetic psychology; Individual development). Study of the changes in cognitive, motivational, psychophysiological, and social functioning that occur throughout the human life span.
Mental development (Intellectual development; Thought process development)
Psychological schools. Freudian, Jungian, Gestalt, dynamic, introspective, etc.
Aptitude. The potential ability of an individual to perform an as yet unlearned task or skill.
Socialization. Process through which individuals internalize the values, beliefs and norms of a society and learn to function as its members.
Social inclusion (Social assimilation; Social cohesion; Social integration)
Information society (Information age; Information revolution; Knowledge society; Learning society)

Social capital (Social networks; Social relations; Social ties). A combination of social norms (such as trusts), social networks, relations and ties held by an individual or predominant within a group.
Social change (Changing society; Social dynamics; Social progress)
Working class (Lower class; Proletariat). A social class comprising those who do manual labour for wage, especially those who do not own any property. Use only when indexing historical works.
Group behaviour (Collective behaviour; Collective psychology; Group psychology)
Social status (Socio-economic status). Position in a community relative to other members of the community.
Modernization. Process of change in a society or social institution in which the most recent ways, ideas or styles are adapted or acquired.
Group dynamics. The way in which members of a group react to each other.
Malnutrition. Includes calorie, protein and/or vitamin deficiencies.
Elderly. Beyond the customary age of retirement.
Homophobia (Anti-gay bias; Discrimination against sexual minorities; Sexual orientation discrimination)
Gender-based violence. Violence directed against a person because of that person’s gender, gender identity or gender expression, or which affects persons of a particular gender disproportionately.
Hate speech (Hate discourse; Online hate speech)
Disadvantaged groups (Groups of concern; Socially disadvantaged; Underprivileged groups; Vulnerable groups)
Disadvantaged children (Marginalized children; Socially disadvantaged children; Underprivileged children)
Social conflicts (Class conflicts; Role conflicts; Social tensions; Social unrest)
Disabled children (Children with disabilities; Handicapped children)
Disadvantaged youth (Socially disadvantaged youth; Underprivileged youth)
Gender minorities (Bisexuals; Gays; Homosexuals; Lesbians; Sexual minorities; Transsexuals)
Child abuse (Battered children; Cruelty to children; Paedophilia)
Counselling (Guidance). Giving advice, information or encouragement to people in need.
Child welfare (Child protection; Child welfare services)
Health services (Community health services; Health care; Medical services; Social medicine)
Social services (Social assistance; Social welfare institutions; Welfare services)
Social welfare (Public welfare; Social protection; Welfare planning; Welfare policy)
Social security (Child allowances; Disability benefits; Family allowances; Health insurance; Social insurance; Unemployment benefits)
Indigenous peoples (Aboriginals; Indigenous populations; Natives; Tribal peoples)
Amerindians (Caribs; North American Indians; South American Indians)
People of African descent (African Americans; African descendants; Afro-Americans; Afro-descendants; Blacks)
Coloureds. Use only with respect to the ethnic group so designated in South Africa.
Ethnic conflicts (Racial conflicts; Racial tensions; Racial violence; Tribal conflicts; Tribalism)
Rural migration (Rural exodus). The migration of rural workers to urban areas.
Return migration (Involuntary return (expulsion); Resettlement; Voluntary return)
Youth (Adolescents; Teenagers; Young persons). Use more specific descriptor.
Sex. The biological characteristics which define humans as female or male.
Ageing population (Ageing society; Population ageing). Continuing increase of elderly population both in absolute and in proportional terms in a given society.
Population distribution. Physical arrangement and location of populations.
Demography. Use for theoretical works dealing with human populations, concerned with their size, structure, distribution, growth and migration.
Migration (International migration; Population migration; Population mobility; Population movement)
Population dynamics (Demographic trends; Population change). Population activity in terms of decline, increase or stabilization.
Brain drain. The loss suffered by a country as a result of the emigration of trained professionals and technicians.
Demographic statistics (Population data; Population statistics; Vital statistics)
Population research (Demographic research). Use for works dealing with research projects. For general works, use "demography".
Population programmes. Activities of international organizations in the population field.

Displaced persons (IDP; Internally displaced persons). Persons who have fled or been driven from their communities to localities within their home country. For persons forced to leave their home country, use "refugees".
Urban spaces. Includes market places, town squares, urban parks, playgrounds, etc.
Urbanization. Population concentration in urban areas as a result of rural migration or due to an increase in the number of urban areas. Do not confuse with "urban development".
Industrial areas. Areas, usually urban, with a relatively high industrial concentration, either planned or unplanned.
Self help. At the community level.
Community centres (CLC; Community learning centres). Local centres for all kinds of academic and recreational activities.

Rural extension (Agricultural extension). Includes training for farmers in more efficient practices, planning and management skills, low-interest credit, simple irrigation, subsidized fertilizer and post-harvest facilities, etc.

Human settlements (Land settlement; Population settlements; Settlement patterns). Consist of shelter, infrastructure, services required by a community for the fulfillment of its functions as a social body.
Communities (Community environment; Local communities; Rural communities; Urban communities)

Cultural landscapes. Illustrative of the evolution of human society and settlement over time, under the influence of the physical constraints/opportunities of the natural environment and of successive social, economic and cultural forces.
Sacred sites. Natural landscapes such as stones, cliffs, mountains, trees, forests, sources, lakes or rivers being regarded as of a marked religious or spiritual significance.
Regional planning. Refers to regions within a country.
Regional economy. Use when referring to regions within a country.
Scientific information (STI; Scientific and technical information; Technical information)
Automatic text analysis (Automatic abstracting; Automatic classification)
Cybernetics. The science of control and communication, specifically the interaction between automatic control and people.
Film strips. A strip of motion picture carrying a still photograph, or other graphic material, on each of its frames. Widely used as an audiovisual instruction tool.
Automatic indexing (Computer assisted indexing; Machine indexing)
Bibliographic standards (Bibliographic record formats; CCF; Catalogue formats; Common Communication Format; MARC; UNIMARC)
ISBD (ISBD (M); ISBD (NBM); ISBD (S)). International standard bibliographic description.

Bibliology (Bibliometrics; Book collecting). The systematic study of the properties and characteristics of books in relation to the publication process or to the techniques of printing, production and marketing.
Computer science (Computer techniques; Computer technology; Informatics)
Classification systems (BLISS classification; BSO classification; Classification research; Classification schemes; Colon classification; Dewey; LCC; UDC)
Information. Data that has been organized in such a way that it achieves meaning, in a generalized way.
Documentation. The continuous and systematic processing of documents or data for specialized information users.
Subject headings. A word, term or a phrase chosen to express a concept or a concept combination in indexing and to constitute an entry.
Terminological control (Vocabulary control). Controls that synonyms and near-synonyms are cross-referenced equivalently and homonyms and polysemes are distinguished by qualifiers.
Science popularization (Scientific initiation; Scientific literacy; Technical literacy; Technological literacy)
Access to information (Accessibility of information; Availability of information; Communication barriers; Information barriers)
Data protection (Computer crime; Computer security; Data privacy; Data security)
Communication administration (Mass media administration; Mass media management)

Public information (Government publicity). Information, offered by governmental and corporate bodies to the public, to disseminate knowledge concerning the programmes and activities of the institution.
Open access. Knowledge resources made available for public access or public consumption at large scale, without any hindrance of subscription fee or access charges.

Open data (Open government data). Practice of publishing (raw) data in a way that is accessible, reusable, machine readable and licensed permissively. Can be generated by a wide range of parties, including public authorities, the semi-public sector, businesses and the public.

Internet governance. The development and application by Governments, the private sector and civil society, in their respective roles, of shared principles, norms, rules, decision-making procedures, and programmes that shape the evolution and use of the Internet.
Media pluralism (Concentration of media ownership). Refers to a sufficient variety of media outlets provided by a range of private, public and non-profit owners.
Media diversity. Refers to the availability of sufficient variety of media content.
Information theory (Coding; Communication theory; Decoding; Messages). Includes the coding and decoding of messages.
Intercultural dialogue (Dialogue among civilizations; Intercultural communication). Verbal and nonverbal communication among people of different cultures.
Communication process (Channels of communication; Communication (thought transfer))
News flow (News; News items; News transmission)
Communication and development. The use of the various forms of physical communications infrastructure and the media in the development process.
Computers and development (Computer science and development; Informatics and development)
Conferences (Congresses; International conferences; Meetings; Symposia). Use only when referring to their organization, financing, etc.
Information user instruction (Bibliographic instruction; Library instruction)
Information needs (Information demand; Information user needs)
Archive finding aids (Archive inventories; Archive registers)
Information/library legislation (Library law; Library legislation; Library regulations)
Information and development. Refers to the contribution of scientific and social science information to the development process.
News agencies (Media outlets; News media organizations; News outlets; News services)
Information scientists (Information officers). A person who works on the theory or application of informatics or information science, i.e. analyses, designs, implements etc. information systems.
Programme content (Broadcasting content; Content analysis; Media content). In the field of communication.
Publishing (Publication (process)). Making a record of knowledge available to the public as a publication.
Postal services (Mail services; Postage stamps; Postal communications)
Community media (Community broadcasting; Community-owned and participatory media; Local broadcasting; Local media)
Radio programmes (Radio drama; Radio games; Radio serials)
Television programmes (Television drama; Television games; Television serials)
Broadcasting industry (Broadcasting corporations; Broadcasting organizations; TV/radio industry)
Press. Newspapers, journals, periodicals, and their publishing.
Editors. A person who is responsible for, or prepares for publication, the contents of a document to which he may or may not have contributed.
Electronic publishing (Computer assisted publishing; Desktop publishing)
Bibliographic services (Abstracting and indexing services; Bibliographic database producers; Current awareness services; Secondary information producers)

Geographical information systems (GIS). An information system containing geographically referenced information for use in decision-making in several domains, most of which relate to the human use of the physical environment.

Digital libraries (Electronic libraries; Virtual libraries). Organized collections of information resources in digital or electronic format along with the services designed to help users identify and use those collections.
Public archives (Public records). (1) In general usage, records accumulated by government agencies. (2) Records open to public inspection by law or custom.
Information services (Documentation centres; Information analysis centres; Information centres; Information units; Referral services)
Scientific information systems (Engineering information systems; Technical information systems)
National libraries. A 'library' which is responsible for acquiring and conserving copies of all significant publications published in the country and may function as a "legal deposit library".
Document delivery (Document supply). Providing users of information with the documents that they request.
Data centres. An organization handling and providing mainly numerical data usually without evaluation.
Educational management information systems (EMIS; Educational information systems)
Abstracts (Abstract journals). The usually non-critical indication of the subject contents of a document, aiming to permit the user a decision about the relevance of the document.
Accessions lists. A list of new acquisitions issued periodically.
Yearbooks. An annual 'volume' of current information in descriptive and/or statistical form, sometimes limited to a special field.
Anthologies. A collection of works of various authors or of one author selected for a specific purpose or under specific aspects.
Machine readable materials. Information coded by methods requiring the use of a computer for processing.

Catalogues (Card catalogues; Catalogs; Computerized catalogues; Library catalogues; OPAC; Online public access catalogues; Union catalogues). An ordered compilation of bibliographic descriptions and sufficient information to afford access to the documents.

Indexes (Citation indexes; Index bulletins; KWIC indexes; KWOC indexes; Periodical indexes; Permuted indexes; Subject indexes). An ordered reference list of the contents of a file or document together with references for identification or location of those contents.
Literature reviews (State of the art reviews). A survey of progress in a particular field of science over a given period.
Primary documents. An original "document" which is not the result of a documentation process.
Conference papers (Conference proceedings; Meeting papers). Use only when referring to their writing, editing, etc.
Monographs. (1) A treatise on a single subject. (2) In cataloguing, any publication which is not "serials".
Documents (Information bearing materials; Information materials; Recorded information; Source materials)
Serials (Series). A publication issued in separate and successive parts usually in a uniform format with constant title and intended to be continued indefinitely.
Directories. A list of persons or organizations systematically or alphabetically arranged giving some information about the single units, usually at least the addresses.
Guides to information sources (Guides to literature sources; Literature guides)
Magnetic tape recordings (Sound cassettes; Tape recordings)

Indexing (Concept analysis; Subject indexing). Assignment of index terms to documents or objects with the aim to be able later on to retrieve the documents or objects according to the selected concepts designated by the index terms (essentially, descriptors).

Selective dissemination of information (Interest profiles; SDI). A service which continually disseminates documents, references, "abstracts" or data selected according to the interest profiles of the users.
Cataloguing (Bibliographic description; Cataloging; Centralized cataloguing; Cooperative cataloguing; Descriptive cataloguing; Metadata)
International circulation of materials. Use only in relation to agreements that aim to facilitate the international exchange of materials intended for educational, scientific and cultural purposes.
Information dissemination. The supply of information or records from a storage point to persons or organizations.
Information processing (Information management; Documentary information processing; Information handling; Information storage and retrieval). The storage and processing of items of information.
Information retrieval (Bibliographic searches; Literature searches; Retrospective searches)
Library circulation (Library loan services). Lending to users the documents requested.

Remote sensing (Sensors; Telemetry). An advanced system of information gathering to monitor and forecast developments on the surface of the earth and identify an area's natural resources by looking at the world from aircraft, balloons, or satellites and evaluating the data gathered.
Open source software (FOSS; Free and open source software)
Artificial intelligence. Capability of a device to perform functions normally associated with human intelligence.
Expert systems (Knowledge based systems). Computer system based on a data base created by human authorities on a particular subject.
Robotics. An area of artificial intelligence applied to the industrial use of robots for performance of repetitive tasks.

Data processing (Data handling; EDP; Electronic data processing; Remote data processing; Signal processing and detection; Teleprocessing). Systematic handling, manipulation, and computation of data, always involving the use of computers. Do not confuse with "information processing".

Information technology (ICT). Includes technology for data base management systems, as well as for information distribution, such as teleprocessing systems, networks of terminals, videotex systems, micrography, etc.
Encoding (Data capture; Keyboarding). "Data transformation" or representation applying a "code".
Telematics (Teleinformatics). Data transfer services via telecommunication systems.
Communication technology (Communication engineering; Telecommunications engineering; Telecommunications technology)
Telecommunications networks (Communication networks (IT); Communication systems (IT); Telecommunications links)
Computer software (Application software; Basic software; Computer programs; Operating systems; Software packages)
Online systems (Interactive online systems; Realtime systems)
Teleconferencing (Computer conferencing; Videoconferencing; Virtual conferencing). Conducting conferences simultaneously at dispersed locations using video, telephone or related media.
Electronic mail (E-mail; Electronic messaging; Messaging systems). Includes message creation, electronic mail and electronic filing.
Digitization (Digital technology). Conversion of paper image or any other traditional document support into electronic image.
Internet (Intranet; LANs; Local area networks; WANs; Wide area networks)
Mobile phones (Cell phones; Cellphones; Cellular phones; Smartphones)
Internet universality. Advocates for an Internet that is based on human Rights, that is Open and Accessible to all, and nurtured by Multistakeholder participation (ROAM principles).
TV/radio equipment (Radio receivers; Radio transmitters; Television cameras; Television receivers; Television transmitters)
Electronic circuits (Circuits; Computer circuits; Digital circuits; Logic and switching circuits)
Microprocessors (Chip). The computer's central processing unit.
Public domain. Publicly accessible information, the use of which does not infringe any legal right, or any obligation of confidentiality.
Courts (Criminal courts; Judiciary; Supreme courts; Tribunals)
Neighbouring rights. Rights of performers, producers of phonograms and broadcasting organizations.
Piracy (Broadcasting piracy; Computer piracy). Unauthorized reproduction, importing or distribution of works protected by copyright or neighbouring rights.
Legal status. The standing of an individual or a group before the law which determines rights and duties.
International law (Private international law; Public international law)
Rights of states (Equality of states; Recognition rights)
International instruments (Charters; International agreements; International conventions; International declarations; International recommendations; Treaties)
Legal systems (Case law; Code Napoleon; Modern law; Primitive law; Roman law)
Consensus. An opinion that all or the majority of a group agree with.
Right to justice (Legal rights; Right to a fair trial)
Gender equality (Gender inequality). Equal rights, responsibilities and opportunities of women and men and girls and boys.
Freedom of association (Right of association; Trade union rights)
Freedom of expression (Right of reply; Right to communicate)
Freedom of speech (Right to freedom of speech)
Freedom of the press (Freedom of the media; Media freedom; Press freedom)
Freedom of movement (Right to freedom of movement)
Freedom of thought (Freedom of conscience; Freedom of opinion)
Right to property (Property law; Property rights)
Collective human rights (Peoples rights; Rights of peoples)
Cultural rights (Access to culture; Cultural freedom; Cultural liberty; Right to cultural identity; Right to culture)
Human rights violations (Abuse of human rights)
Humanitarian law (International humanitarian law; Law of armed conflicts; Law of war; Rights of civilians; Rights of war prisoners; Rights of war wounded)
Rights of special groups. Do not use as a descriptor.
Governance. Manner in which power and authority are exercised by both public and private bodies. Includes such issues as public sector management, legal framework, accountability and transparency.
Women in politics. Women as office-holders, political party functionaries, etc. For political participation of women in general, use "womens participation" and "politics", or "womens suffrage".
Regionalism. Use only in a subnational context.
Politics (Political development; Political life; Political reform)

Electronic governance (E-governance; Online governance). The public sector's use of information and communication technologies with the aim of improving information and service delivery, encouraging citizen participation in the decision-making process and making government more accountable, transparent and effective.
Civic engagement (Civic participation; Popular participation; Public participation). Any individual or group activity addressing issues of public concern.
Political power (Executive power; Judicial power; Legislative power)
Global public goods. A public good with benefits that are strongly universal in terms of countries, people and both current and future generations.
South South relations. Relations among developing countries.
Regional organizations (International regional organizations). Groupings of countries for economic, political, or military purposes.

Peacekeeping (Peacekeeping forces; Peacekeeping operations). Action linked with the deployment of UN military and/or police personnel in areas of instability, with the consent of all the parties concerned.
Peace agreements. Agreements, not necessarily in written form, between parties within a country.
Foreign aid. Aid from the viewpoint of the donor country.
Armed forces (Army; Military forces; Military personnel; Soldiers)
Humanitarian assistance (Humanitarian action; Humanitarian aid). Any material assistance or intercession by the international community in troubled areas for purely humanitarian ends.
Global commons. Resources or zones that are shared as common property by all nations.
Regional cooperation. Cooperation for development in any economic, social or technical field at the supranational level.
International politics (Geopolitics; International affairs; World politics)
Peacemaking. Action to bring hostile parties to agreement through means foreseen in chapter VI of the UN Charter concerning the peaceful settlement of disputes.
Peacebuilding. Action to identify and support structures which will tend to strengthen peace in order to avoid a relapse into conflict.
International cooperation (International assistance). All forms of cooperation on an international basis.
Income. Income of an individual or an organization. Otherwise use "national income".
Gross national product. The output of goods and services in a given country.
Remittances. Transfer of funds by emigrants or migrant workers to their country or region of origin.
Green economy (Green growth; Sustainable economy). Economy which is low-carbon, resource efficient, and socially inclusive.
Structural adjustment. Government austerity measures directed towards altering the structure of the economy.
Comparative advantage. A country's ability to provide certain products and services relatively more cheaply than other products or services.

International division of labour. Theory and practice of international planning and agreements by which countries specialize in the production of those commodities for which they have the greatest comparative advantage. Do not confuse with "division of labour".
Informal sector (Black economy; Informal economy; Unofficial economy). Refers to the unofficial, or non-registered and untaxed, therefore informal, sector of the economy.
Economic relations. Refers only to bilateral relations between countries.
Economic recession (Deflation; Economic crisis; Economic depression)
Economic equilibrium (Equilibrium theory). A state of balance between the various economic forces.
Microeconomics. That part of the study of economics devoted to the behaviour of people, governments and organizations in specific markets.
Capital intensity. Relatively greater plant and equipment costs than labour costs.
Labour intensity. Relatively greater labour costs than plant and equipment costs.
Common markets. Agreement between two or more countries to abolish restrictions on the movement of capital and labour as well as trade restrictions among themselves.
Business cycles (Economic fluctuations). Alternate expansion and contraction in overall economic activity.
Income and wealth. Use more specific descriptor.
Interdependence (Economic interdependence). Mutual economic dependence among countries. For active efforts to promote closer economic ties, use "economic cooperation", "economic integration", etc.
Economic cooperation. Includes cooperative measures in banking, trade, industry etc., between and among countries.
Socio-economic indicators (Cost of living index; Economic indicators)
Dependence (Dependency theory; Economic dependence). Situation in which a country's economy is subordinated to the development of another country's economy.
Macroeconomics. An economic study devoted to examining the function of a country's or region's economy or the international economy as a whole.
Economic structure. Relative importance of the various sectors of the economy.
Economic integration (Regional integration). At the international level.
Capacity building (Capacity development). Implies the enhancement of capabilities of people and institutions to improve their competence and problem solving capacities in a sustainable manner.
Tied aid (Conditional aid). The practice of requiring that funds provided to a developing country be used to procure goods and services in the donor country.
Reconstruction (Post-conflict reconstruction). Recovery and rehabilitation activities following war or large scale devastation.
Human security. Protecting the vital core of all human lives in ways that enhance human freedoms and human fulfilment
Economic reintegration (Economic and social reintegration). Use for ex-combatants and returning civilians.
Development policy. A definite course or method of action selected from among development alternatives. Use more specific descriptors where appropriate.
Financial aid (Capital aid; Financial assistance; Financial support)
Private aid. Aid provided by churches, foundations, etc.
Endogenous development. Based on the socio-cultural characteristics of a country, rather than on its integration into the world economy.
