Empowerment. Enabling individuals or communities to take charge and make full use of their knowledge, energies and judgment.
Self reliance (Alternative development). Reliance primarily on a country's own human and natural resources and the capacity for autonomous goal-setting and decision-making.

Basic needs (Human needs). The minimum requirements for a decent standard of life: adequate food, shelter, clothing, community services. They also include needs relating to human rights, public participation in decision-making, productive employment.

Human development (People centered development). A process of enlarging people's choices: focuses on both the formation of human capabilities - improved health, knowledge and skills - and the use people make of their acquired capabilities, for work or leisure.
Participatory development (Grassroots development; Local development). Institutionalization of popular participation in the development process.
Civil society. Organized and legally bound social life that is voluntary and autonomous from the State, such as nongovernmental organizations, associations and grassroot movements.
Integrated development. Development taking into account a range of factors characteristic of the human condition.

Development theory. A highly interdisciplinary field involving all the social sciences, in addition to economics, also sociology and anthropology, demography, geography, health research, education, agricultural and other natural sciences, etc.
Economic and social development (Development; Economic development; Social development). Use more specific descriptor when appropriate.
Technical cooperation (Technical assistance). Transfer of skills and provision of advice to developing countries in various fields: administrative, scientific, professional, and technical.

Sustainable development (Ecodevelopment; Environmental sustainability). Environmentally sound development, which meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Development indicators. Numerical data used as benchmarks in the formulation and monitoring of development policy.
Development strategies. The coordinated package of programmes and projects dictated by development policy, which aims to achieve a particular kind of development.
Feasibility studies. They identify and prepare a preliminary design of the technical and institutional alternatives that may exist for a proposed project.
Women and development. Integration of women into the development process.
Sea fishing (Coastal fishing; Deep sea fishing; Marine fishing)

Agrarian structure (Agrarian systems). A complex of relationships which exist among land tenure, production and supporting services, and related rural institutions, each constituting an integral part of the wider whole.
Winemaking (Oenology; Vinification; Wine making; Wine production)
Food security. Access by all people at all times to enough food for an active, healthy life.
Agroforestry (Agrisilviculture; Forest farming). Simultaneous growing of trees with food crops and/or livestock on the same piece of land.
Forest management (Afforestation; Reforestation). Refers to timber extraction and reforestation aspects of forestry.
Dry farming (Dry land agriculture). A system of producing crops in arid and semi-arid regions without the use of irrigation.
Agronomy. The science of crop and soil management.
Industrialization (Industrial revolution). Refers to the initial stage of industrial development.
Agroindustry (Agricultural industry). The integration of agricultural production, processing and marketing under a single comprehensive management.
Sea bed mining (Deep sea mining; Offshore drilling; Underwater mining; Underwater oil and gas extraction)
Irrigation (Irrigation canals; Irrigation engineering; Irrigation systems)
Civil engineering. Use for construction work other than buildings.
Mining (Metal mining; Mines; Mining engineering; Mining industries)
Genetically modified organisms (GMOs; Genetically engineered organisms; Genetically modified crops; Genetically modified food)
Geoengineering (Climate engineering). Refers to a broad set of methods and technologies that aim to deliberately alter the climate system in order to alleviate the impacts of climate change.
Green chemistry. Design of products and processes that reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.
Metalworking. Includes forging, forming, sheet metalworking, drawing, extrusion, rolling, tube-making, etc.
Automatic control. Production in which all controls are automatically carried out by machinery.
Fuel technology (Coal technology; Gas technology; Petroleum technology)
Pharmaceutical technology. Includes drugs, toiletries and cosmetics technology.
Human machine interaction (Human computer interface; Man machine systems)

Biotechnology (Bioengineering; Biological engineering; Genetic engineering). Utilization of biological organisms, processes and systems to make or modify products, to improve plants or animals, or to develop microorganisms for specific uses.
Ergonomics (Human engineering; Human factors engineering). The optimal adaptation of the work environment to human needs.
Production engineering (Industrial engineering; Production processes; Production technology)
Petroleum (Crude oils; Fossile fuels; Gasoline; Mineral oils)
Adobe bricks (Adobe construction; Sun baked bricks)
Petroleum products (Bitumens; Petrochemicals). Includes light oils, gas oils, fuel oils, greases, etc.
Commodities (Primary products). As opposed to semi-manufactured or finished products, materials in their original state, or processed only enough to be prepared for marketing in international trade.
Space stations (Space observatories). Includes orbiting space stations, lunar bases, etc.
Nuclear weapons (Atomic bomb; Atomic weapons; Weapons of mass destruction)
Foreign investment (FDI; Foreign capital; Foreign direct investment)
Branding (Brand names; Corporate identity; Emblems; Logos; Visual identity)
Debt relief (Debt for equity swap; Debt for nature swap; Debt refinancing; Debt renegotiation; Debt reorganization; Debt rescheduling). Use with respect to a country's external public debt.

Terms of trade. The ratio of export to import prices of the products involved in a given country or region's international trade. May also be used by extension with respect to trade between areas within a country, such as urban or rural areas.
Microcredit (Microfinance). Appropriate small-scale financial support for poverty alleviation.
Debts (Liabilities (economic)). Use more specific descriptor where appropriate.
Public debt. Refers to both internal and external indebtedness.
Work study (Time study; Work measurement). Detailed examination of the manner in which a particular job is performed, with a view to rationalizing performance and increasing productivity.
Knowledge management. Development of new knowledge or absorption of existing knowledge, its organization and diffusion with the overall aim of optimizing results.
Stakeholders (Constituency). An individual, group, institution, or government with an interest or concern in a particular measure taken or a proposal made by an organization.
Risk management (Business continuity planning; Contingency planning; Disaster recovery planning; ERM; Enterprise risk management; Institutional risk management; Risk assessment; Risk evaluation)
Operations research. Application of scientific methods to the analysis of problems so as to provide optimum solutions for decision making.
Youth organizations (Scouting; Youth clubs). Organizations outside school.
Decentralization. Dispersion or distribution of functions and powers from a central authority to a local authority or community.

Quality circles. A group of workers, performing similar work and trained to identify and solve problems, who volunteer to make recommendations relating to the improvement of productivity, quality, work morale, etc.
Management. Use in connection with three main tasks: supervision of and responsibility for the work of others, allocating labour, material and capital to produce a high return, and decision making.
Joint ventures. Project involving enterprises or organizations that combine theory, know-how, capital and/or labour to reach a common objective.

Transnational corporations (International business enterprises; Multinational enterprises). Companies operating in a number of countries but with service and even production facilities frequently located outside those countries.
Job evaluation (Job classification; Post classification; Post evaluation)
Leave (Absenteeism; Holidays from work; Leave of absence; Maternity leave; Sick leave)
Professional personnel (Professional staff; Professionals; Specialists). For more specific descriptors, see "occupations" and "personnel".
Quality of working life (Humanization of work)
Occupational qualifications (Job requirements; Skill requirements). The combined aptitudes and skills which permit someone to take up a job.
Occupational status (Professional status). Employment rank, position or status achieved by an individual or group.

Conditions of employment (Labour contract). Use for the conditions of employment stipulated in the staff regulations of an enterprise or organization, or in a collective agreement negotiated by employer's and workers' representatives.
Labour standards. Standards concerning employment and working conditions set out in collective agreements between employers and workers or in labour laws and regulations adopted by the legislature.
Working conditions (Labour conditions). The physical, social and managerial factors affecting a worker's job environment.
Recruitment. Policies and procedures for seeking qualified employees.
Career development. The continuous planning carried out to advance a person's career based on experience and on any training undertaken to upgrade qualifications or to acquire new ones.

Personnel management (Human resources management; Personnel administration; Staff management). Refers to all management decisions affecting the nature of the relationship between the organization and its employees, i.e. its human resources.
Occupational psychology (Industrial psychology). The application of psychology to the work environment and personnel management.

Occupational sociology (Industrial sociology; Sociology of work). Sociology applied to the world of work, e.g. the workplace as a social system, occupational status, intergroup relations in the enterprise, etc.
Job description (Job analysis; Task analysis). Recognized list of functions and tasks included in a particular job.
Working time (Hours of work; Working time arrangement)
Office workers (Clerical workers; White collar workers)
Manpower (Labour force; Working population). The economically active population.
Labour mobility. Ability of individual workers to move in and among labour markets.
Labour supply. Denotes not only the size of the workforce, but also its skills and geographic location as well as its willingness and ability to be productive.
Workers participation (Employee participation; Industrial democracy; Joint management; Workers management)

Structural unemployment (Technical unemployment; Technological unemployment). Caused by changes in the structure of the economy resulting from such factors as technological change or relocation of industry, or by changes in the composition of the labour force.
Manpower needs (Labour demand; Labour requirements). General demand for labour, or demand in particular industries or sectors of the economy.
Human resources (Human capital). The actual workforce (manpower), plus the potential workforce.
Collective agreements. Agreement concerning the working conditions of a particular group of workers concluded between the workers' representatives and the employers.

Collective bargaining. The process by which representatives of employers and employees discuss and negotiate the various phases of their relationship with a view to arriving at a mutually acceptable labour agreement.
Employment creation (Job creation). The generation of new jobs in sectors or enterprises requiring more manpower.

Labour relations (Industrial relations; Labour-management relations). Collective relations between employers and employees, between employers and trade unions, or between employers, unions and the government. Use "personnel management" for individual relations between employers and employees.
Division of labour. The process whereby labour is allocated to the activity in which it is most productive.
Gender division of labour (Sexual division of labour)
Labour productivity. Efficiency of production at the level of the individual, the enterprise or the specific economic sector.
Employment services (Manpower services; Placement services). Services provided officially by governments as well as those run on a private fee-paying basis.
Manpower planning (Employment planning; Labour planning). Analysis and projection of current manpower needs as well as future needs in light of long-term economic planning.
Africa South of the Sahara (Subsaharan Africa)
South Sudan. Use for events after 9 July 2011. For earlier events use Sudan.
Congo DR (Democratic Republic of the Congo). Use for events after May 1997, otherwise, use Zaire.
Zaire. Use for events before May 1997, otherwise, use "Congo DR".
Curaçao. Use for events after 10 October 2010. For earlier events use Netherlands Antilles.
Sint Maarten (Sint Maarten (Dutch part)). Use for events after 10 October 2010. For earlier events use Netherlands Antilles.
Netherlands Antilles. Use for events before 10 October 2010. For later events, use as appropriate, Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten, or Netherlands.
Saint Kitts and Nevis (Saint Christopher and Nevis)
Hong Kong. Use for events before 1 July 1997. Otherwise, use Hong Kong China.
Hong Kong China. Use for events after 1 July 1997. Otherwise, use Hong Kong
Iran, Islamic Republic. Use for events after 1979. For earlier events, use Iran.
Korea R (Republic of Korea; South Korea). Use for events after 1948.
Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR; Laos)
Macao. Use for events before 20 Dec. 1999. Otherwise, use Macao, China
Macao, China. Use for events after 20 Dec. 1999. Otherwise, use Macao.
Samoa. For events before September 1997, use Western Samoa.
Serbia. Use for events after 3 June 2006. For events between 4 February 2003 and 3 June 2006, use Serbia and Montenegro. For earlier events, use Yugoslavia.
Montenegro. Use for events after 3 June 2006. For events between 4 February 2003 and 3 June 2006 use Serbia and Montenegro. For earlier events use Yugoslavia.
Czech Republic (Czechia). Use for events after 1992.
North Macedonia (Macedonia; The former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia)
Belarus. Use for events after 1991. Otherwise, use "Byelorussian SSR".
Central and Eastern Europe (Central Europe; Eastern Europe)
German DR. Use for events between 1949 and 1990.
Germany. Use for events before 1949 and after October 1990.
Germany FR. Use for events between 1949 and 1990.
Moldova R (Republic of Moldova). Use for events after 1991. For earlier events, use Moldavian SSR
Russian Federation. Use for events after 1991.
Serbia and Montenegro. Use for events between 4 February 2003 and 3 June 2006. For earlier events, use Yugoslavia.
UK (England; Great Britain; Northern Ireland; Scotland; United Kingdom; United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; Wales)
Yugoslavia. Use for events before 4 February 2003. Otherwise, use Serbia and Montenegro.
ASEAN countries. Member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations
EEC countries. Use for events before November 1993. Otherwise, use "European Union".
European Union. Use for events after November 1993. Otherwise, use "EEC countries".
E-9 countries (E9 countries; Nine High-Population Countries)
CMEA countries. Council for Mutual Economic Assistance. Use for historical references only.
Developed countries (AIC; Advanced industrial countries; Industrialized countries)

unesco_fr.http://vocabularies.unesco.org/thesaurus: Communication. Processus social interactif qui implique le partage d'information, d'expérience et de culture, à la fois concrètement et électroniquement, pour l'enrichissement mutuel de toutes les personnes concernées. Utiliser un descripteur plus précis.
Recherche sur le terrain (Travail de terrain; Travail sur le terrain)
RSS d'Estonie. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.
URSS (Union soviétique). S'applique aux événements survenus entre 1922 et 1991.
Stratégie d'interrogation. Analyse et formulation des meilleures méthodes au moyen desquelles un système de recherche documentaire peut répondre à une question.
Recherche d'information en ligne (Recherche documentaire en ligne; Recherche en ligne)
Organisation de la recherche (Coordination de la recherche)
Diplômé (Finissant; Gradué). Personne ayant répondu aux exigences d'un programme d'études supérieures et qui s'est vu décerner un diplôme.
Étudiant non diplômé. Étudiant engagé dans des études menant à un grade de premier cycle, p. ex. à un baccalauréat.
Études sociales. Adaptation de la connaissance issue des sciences sociales à des fins d'enseignement aux niveaux primaire et secondaire.
Groupe ethnique (Appartenance ethnique; Ethnisme; Groupe racial; Minorité ethnique; Minorité nationale; Minorité raciale; Origine ethnique; Race)

Gestion de dossiers (Administration de documents; Destruction de documents; Disposition des documents; Maintenance des documents; Élimination de documents). Secteur de la gestion administrative générale responsable de l'organisation économique et efficace des opérations liées à la création, l'utilisation et la maintenance, ainsi que la disposition des documents.
Exilé. Individu chassé de son pays d'origine par une autorité officielle pour des raisons politiques.
Marché financier (Bourse; Bourse des valeurs; Bourse des valeurs mobilières; Marché boursier; Marché des capitaux)
Sylviculture. Secteur de la foresterie qui s'occuppe du développement, de la reproduction et de la garde des arbres forestiers.
Forme musicale (Symphonie). Comprend les concertos, les sonates, les symphonies, etc.
Congé d'études (Congé de formation; Congé-formation). Utiliser quand il s'agit d'un congé, rémunéré ou non, accordé à un employé à des fins éducatives.
Formation préalable des enseignants (Formation d'adaptation à l'emploi des enseignants; Formation initiale des enseignants)
Service éducatif itinérant (Classe mobile; Salle de classe mobile; École mobile)
Cours d'enseignement (Cours de formation). Aspects administratifs des programmes de cours. Utiliser un descripteur plus précis.
Organisation des fichiers (Organisation de la mémoire; Structure des fichiers)
Mutation (Changement biologique; Variation génétique). Tout changement dans le génotype d'un organisme intervenant au niveau des gènes, des chromosomes ou du génome.
Génétique (Génomique). Etude des modèles de transmission héréditaire de traits spécifiques.
RSS de Géorgie. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.

Mondialisation. Transnationalisation, axée sur le marché, des relations économiques (commerce, investissement étranger, flux financier), conduisant à l'accroissement de l'interdépendance économique et réduisant en conséquence la capacité des gouvernements à contrôler l'économie nationale.
Relations économiques internationales (Économie internationale; Économie mondiale)
Mesure de sécurité (Mesure de protection; Mesure de prévention; Mesure de sûreté)
Eau souterraine (Eau de fond; Nappe souterraine)
Technicien. En deça du niveau professionnel mais au-delà des niveaux du secrétariat ou du travail manuel.
Logement (Abri; Demeure; Domicile; Habitation; Hébergement; Refuge; Résidence)
Gestion des ressources en eau (Aménagement des ressources en eau; Gestion des ressources hydrauliques; Gestion des ressources hydriques; Mise en valeur des ressources en eau)
Roche (Mécanique des roches; Pierre (roche); Propriété des roches)
Acoustique (Onde acoustique; Onde sonore; Son; Vibration)
Sélection des livres (Commande de livres; Sélection de documents; Triage de revues)
Bon UNESCO. Destiné à l'achat de publications et de matériels audiovisuels pour favoriser la réalisation d'objectifs éducatifs, scientifiques et culturels.
Système d'information (Système d'information documentaire; Système documentaire)
Conflit international (Contentieux international; Différend international; Litige international)
Stage de formation (Programme de formation). Cours organisé dans un environnement professionnel pendant ou à la fin d'un processus éducatif.
Transport. Se réfère à la fois aux systèmes de transport et au transport de marchandises. Utiliser un descripteur plus précis si possible.
Activité solaire (Perturbation solaire; Tache solaire). Inclue le vent solaire, les éruptions, les protubérances et les taches solaires.
RSS de Kazakhstan. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.

Droit de la mer (Droit international de la mer; Droit maritime international)
RSS de Lettonie. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.
RSS de Lituanie. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.

Programme d'éducation. Série d'activités planifiées, d'un point de vue administratif, en rapport avec le développement d'une institution. Ne pas confondre avec "programme d'enseignement".

Population. Se réfère uniquement à la population d'un pays particulier ou d'une région. Autrement, utiliser un descripteur plus précis quand c'est opportun.

Restauration (Restauration d'oeuvres d'art; Restauration de monuments; Technique de restauration)
RSS d'Ukraine. S'applique aux événements survenus avant 1991.

Langue amérindienne (Langue indienne d'Amérique centrale; Langue indienne d'Amérique du Nord; Langue indienne d'Amérique du Sud)

Archives de l'administration locale (Archives communales; Archives municipales)
Archives gouvernementales (Archives diplomatiques; Archives militaires; Archives officielles)
RSS d'Arménie. S'applique à des événements survenus avant 1991.
Oeuvre d'art (Artefact; Objet d'art; Travail d'artiste)
Théorie de l'art. Utiliser un descripteur plus précis quand c'est pertinent.

Atelier (méthode pédagogique). Réunion d'individus, généralement des experts, partageant les mêmes intérêts et les mêmes problèmes, pour favoriser les échanges d'information et acquérir des habiletés et des techniques utiles.
Phonothèque (Archives audio; Archives de disques; Archives phonographiques; Archives sonores; Sonothèque)
Vérification de la gestion. Évaluation systématique des méthodes de gestion par des équipes de l'intérieur ou de l'extérieur d'une organisation.

Langage d'indexation (Langage de recherche documentaire; Langage documentaire). Langage artificiel utilisé dans les systèmes d'information documentaire à des fins d'indexation.

Personnel enseignant paraprofessionnel (Conseiller d'orientation; Personnel d'orientation scolaire; Personnel de soutien scolaire). Comprend le personnel non enseignant occupant des postes professionnels.
Avantages accessoires (Avantages annexes; Avantages complémentaires; Avantages indirects; Bénéfices marginaux)
Salaire (Détermination du salaire; Honoraire; Paye; Rémunération; Traitement). Paiement effectué pour un travail accompli.

Bibliographie (Bibliographie internationale). Liste imprimée de documents décrits dans leur aspect formel.
Bibliographie nationale. Bibliographie des livres publiés sur le territoire d'un pays quelle qu'en soit la langue, et/ou des ouvrages écrits dans la langue du pays.
Bibliothèque institutionnelle (Bibliothèque d'institution; Bibliothèque de bord; Bibliothèque de prison)
Bibliothèque spécialisée. Bibliothèque spécialisée dans une discipline ou un domaine particuliers.
Bibliothèque publique. Bibliothèque desservant gratuitement ou pour une somme minime la population d'une communauté ou d'une région.

Biogenèse. Théorie d'après laquelle tout être vivant est issu d'un autre être vivant.
Industrie du livre (Fabrication du livre; Production du livre)

Bosniaque. Utiliser pour les ouvrages traitant de la langue propre aux bosniaques. Pour les ouvrages traitant de la langue des serbes, des croates et des bosniaques en tant qu'entité, utiliser "serbocroate".
Contribution budgétaire (Campagne de financement; Collecte de fonds; Contribution annoncée; Contribution volontaire). Se réfère tant à la contribution volontaire qu'à la contribution obligatoire.
Opération de construction. Comprend le briquetage, la menuiserie, le plâtrage, le vernissage, la décoration, etc.
RSS de Biélorussie. S'applique aux événements survenus avant 1991, utiliser autrement "Bélarus".

Végétation. Vie végétale caractéristique d'une zone écologique. S'il s'agit de taxonomie, utiliser "flore".

Citation (Extrait). Note de référence à un ouvrage dont on cite un passage entre guillements ou à un matériel source quelconque faisant autorité, présentée pour appuyer une affirmation ou une proposition.

Club (Cinéclub; Club Internet; Club de cinéma; Club de lecture; Club de sport; Club du livre; Vidéoclub)

Thésaurus (Descripteur; Thésaurus monolingue; Thésaurus multilingue; Thésaurus unilingue). Langage documentaire contrôlé et dynamique contenant des termes sémantiquement et génériquement reliés, lequel couvre de manière exhaustive un domaine spécifique de la connaissance.

Croate. Utiliser pour les ouvrages traitant de la langue propre aux croates. Pour les travaux traitant de la langue des serbes, des croates et des bosniaques en tant qu'entité, utiliser "serbocroate".

Droit (Science juridique). S'emploie pour des ouvrages se rapportant à la science du droit. Pour ce qui concerne des lois spécifiques, utiliser "législation", "législation de l'environnement", etc.

Glossaire. Lexique dont les mots ne sont pas nécessairement classés par ordre alphabétique, donnant la définition et l'explication de chacun des termes.

Direction par objectifs (Détermination des objectifs; Fixation des objectifs; Établissement des objectifs). Détermination de buts à atteindre dans une organisation afin de réaliser un meilleur rendement.
Enregistrement sur disque (Disque compact; Disque vinyle)
Enregistrement sonore (Disque enregistré; Document sonore; Matériel audio; Phonogramme)
Enseignement à domicile (École à domicile; École à la maison). Enseignement dispensé comme solution alternative à l'éducation formelle ou donné à des personnes confinées à domicile.
Éducation familiale. Éducation au sein de et par la famille.
